messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations you should know: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on freeways, 35 mph on expressways, 25 mph on city streets (unless posted). | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and yield at yield signs. | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Do not pass on the right unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Headlights** | • Must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Toll Roads** | • Many toll roads require an electronic transponder (e‑Tag). | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in no‑stop zones. | | **Traffic Cameras & Speed Cameras** | • Speed cameras enforce speed limits; violations result in fines. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display valid registration and proof of insurance. | | **Roadside Safety** | • Keep a safe distance from emergency vehicles and follow police instructions. | ### Quick Tips - **Check the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** website for specific local ordinances. - **Use the Texas Highway Patrol’s “Know Your Rights” guide** for detailed explanations of enforcement practices. - **Download the TxDOT mobile app** for real‑time traffic alerts and road conditions. If you need more detailed information on a specific law or want to see how these rules are enforced in practice, let me know!
